title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO and AI hardware stages its biggest one-day rebound of the selloff
intro: Nvidia's board brought Jensen Huang back as chief executive on Monday with White House backing, and US chip, optics, neocloud and equipment stocks surged as the Nasdaq rose more than 6%. Asian governments moved over the weekend to steady markets after last week's rout, but Korea, Taiwan and Shenzhen closed before the US rally while Tokyo was shut for a holiday.
movers_note: Against the Friday Nov 20 close the tracked total rose 10.24% to $26.65T (10.37% across the 56 companies with a newer quote; about $210B of TSMC's gain is a market cap restated on the source), and it is down 1.04% from the Monday Nov 16 close a week earlier; Nvidia (+31.5%), Astera Labs (+23.2%), Credo (+22.6%), CoreWeave (+22.3%) and ASE (+21.4%) gained most, while Samsung (−3.1%), SK hynix (−2.5%), Foxconn (−1.9%), KYEC (−0.3%) and Microsoft (+1.6%) lagged.

items.headline: Nvidia's board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, effective immediately
items.summary: The board voted unanimously to return Huang to the president, CEO and director roles, with Colette Kress continuing as CFO after her stint as interim chief. It is keeping the independent-director investigation open, adding a national security and export-control committee, and searching for a chief compliance officer.

items.headline: Nasdaq surges 6.5% as Huang's return sparks a sharp rebound in chip and AI stocks
items.summary: The S&P 500 closed up 4.73% and the Nasdaq Composite up 6.51%. Nvidia rose 31%, CoreWeave 22%, Micron 19% and AMD nearly 7%, and the SMH semiconductor ETF gained more than 16%.

items.headline: Trump says Huang's return poses no national security risk and urges Nvidia to keep reviewing export compliance
items.summary: In a Truth Social post the president said the government sees no security risk in Huang resuming the CEO job, after telling PBS over the weekend that Huang had done nothing wrong. He also told Nvidia to continue its review of compliance with US chip export controls.

items.headline: Seoul, Taipei and Beijing move to steady markets after the AI-led rout
items.summary: South Korea is preparing its 10.76 trillion won market stabilization fund and loosening buyback limits from Nov. 24, Taiwan barred short sales below the prior close and raised short-sale margins, and China will cut minimum margin ratios to 80% from Nov. 30. Taiwan's index fell 17.5% last week before turning higher on Monday.

items.headline: ASE and SPIL tipped to overtake Amkor in 2027 as server-CPU packaging moves beyond CoWoS
items.summary: DigiTimes reports that advanced-packaging capacity remains tight and that TSMC's fully booked CoWoS lines are reserved first for AI accelerator customers, pushing server-CPU packaging work toward ASE and its SPIL unit.
